newsitem.title: USA: US, Japan "very far apart" on insurance - Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: US, Japan "very far apart" on insurance - Sakakibara.

text.p: The United States and Japan are still "very far apart" on how to open Japan's insurance market, and high-level decisions were needed to resolve the deadlock, Tokyo's chief negotiator said on Saturday.

"Frankly, there will have to be considerably large political decisions from both sides to resolve this issue," Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of Japan's Finance Ministry, told reporters after the two countries concluded their two-day talks without a breakthrough.
He said insurance talks had so many political problems that a ministerial meeting between U.S. Trade representatitve Charlene Barshefsky and Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka was necessary.

"It is an issue that cannot be resolved at the working level," Sakakibara said, adding that a date for such a top-level meeting had yet to be determined due to the tight schedule of both Barshefsky and Mitsuzuka.
While acknowleding the gaps still to be filled, Sakakibara stressed that a Dec.15 target date still had very large importance.
"I personally think this will have to be met," he said.
